objective.statement: Understand how bar-lines divide music into bars of equal length.
successCriteria: I know a bar-line is a vertical line across the stave.
I know every bar in a piece holds the same number of beats.
I can place bar-lines and finish with a double bar-line.

explanation.text: Music is divided into short, equal sections called bars. Between one bar and the next we draw a vertical line called a bar-line.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of four-beat music in 4/4, each holding the same number of beats, divided by a bar-line and ending with a double bar-line.

explanation.caption: Two bars of 4/4. Each holds four beats, and the piece ends with a double bar-line.

explanation.text: The time signature at the start tells us how many beats go in each bar. Every bar holds exactly that many beats, never more and never fewer.
At the very end of a piece we draw a double bar-line, with a thin line followed by a thick one.
The first beat of a bar is usually the strongest. Count 'ONE two three four, ONE two three four' and the bar-lines fall just before each ONE.

music.textAlternative: Three bars in 4/4: two crotchets and a minim, two minims, and a semibreve. Each bar lasts four beats.

steps: Press Play all and count 'one, two, three, four' in each bar.
Notice every bar fills exactly four beats, even though the notes inside are different.
The bar-line falls where the count starts again on 'one'.
The double bar-line at the end shows that the music has finished.
demonstration.textAlternative: Three bars of 4/4 music of different notes that each add up to four beats, ending with a double bar-line.

1.reason: Add up the beats in the bar you chose and compare with the time signature: it does not match.

feedback.correct: Yes: that bar holds exactly the right number of beats.

mistakes.bar-overfull: This bar holds more beats than the time signature allows. Count the beats again and remove the extra.
mistakes.bar-underfull: There's still room in this bar. Count how many beats are missing.
mistakes.grouping-obscures-beat: The beats add up, but it's hard to see where each beat starts. Regroup the notes so every beat is visible.
mistakes.unnecessary-tie: You can write those tied notes as a single note (or a dotted note). That's easier to read.
mistakes.rest-grouping: Each silent beat (or part-beat) normally gets its own rest. Split the silence along the beats.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Check the beat total first, then how the notes are grouped.
